ready1_open_rewrite.title: Multi-Physics open-ended question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: In the position-time graph (x-t graph) of a particle undergoing uniformly accelerated rectilinear motion, P(t1, x1) is a point on the graph. PQ is the tangent line through point P, intersecting the x-axis at point Q(0, x2). It is known that when t=0, the magnitude of the particle's velocity is v0. Use t1, x1, x2 and v0 to express the magnitude of the particle's acceleration.
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: The magnitude of the particle's acceleration is $\frac{x_{1}-x_{2}}{t_{1}^{2}}-\frac{v_{0}}{t_{1}}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the graph, the vertical axis is position x, and the horizontal axis is time t. The coordinates of point P on the curve are marked by dashed lines as (t1, x1); the tangent drawn through P is extended leftward and cuts off position x2 at the vertical axis where t=0, that is, Q corresponds to (0, x2). Therefore, expressed according to the problem statement, the magnitude of the acceleration is (x1-x2)/t1^2-v0/t1.
